### Fixed
- **The model pods reach the Hugging Face download CDN: the model-serving egress admits `us.aws.cdn.hf.co`, three labels under `hf.co`** (giantswarm/agent-platform#522; proof 1 of giantswarm/giantswarm#37639). The connectivity chart's `-model-serving-predictor`, `-model-serving-llmisvc-workload` and `-model-serving-download` CiliumNetworkPolicies admitted `huggingface.co`, `*.huggingface.co`, `*.hf.co` and `*.*.hf.co`; Cilium's `*` matches one label and never a dot, so the download CDN the Hub redirects every shard request of a Xet-backed repository to (Xet client or not — the LFS path lands on the same host) matched nothing and the download's SYNs were dropped one second after the DNS proxy had resolved it: with Xet off (#520) the storage-initializer crash-looped on `us.aws.cdn.hf.co`, with Xet on it hung. `modelServing.networkPolicy.huggingFace.fqdns` and `modelManager.networkPolicy.huggingFace.fqdns` gain `*.*.*.hf.co`; the lists stay a `toFQDNs` allow-list (no `world`, no CIDR). `tests/verify-model-serving-policies.py` (`make verify-model-serving-policies`) matches the names of the download path — the Hub, the LFS fronts, the Xet fronts, the CDN and a regional sibling — against the rendered patterns of all three policies with Cilium's rule and keeps out a deeper name and a look-alike domain, so a new host shape fails the render, not a download on an installation. The `modelServing.policies.env` comment of #520 is corrected: Xet off keeps the initializer on one host path that fails fast on a policy drop; it is not what reaches the CDN.
